proposal.summary: Add one reusable evidence-cache skill. Decline the empty-output and stalled-search signals because this snapshot does not establish a submission failure or unproductive search loop.

edits.title: Reuse fetched evidence across single and batched research
edits.content: When research combines single and batched fetching, keep a URL-keyed cache of fetched text. Deduplicate discovered URLs and exclude already cached URLs before batching. Associate batch results with URLs in input order, retain successful evidence, and exclude fetch failures from extraction. Build the extraction evidence directly from cached URL/text pairs so subsequent extraction and citation checks reuse the same text without another fetch. Validate each cited URL against the cache and each nonempty quote by exact substring membership in its corresponding page. Cache reuse and local validation are intermediate successes; verify final submission separately.

additional_candidates.description: URL-keyed caching connects deduplicated single/batched fetching, grouped extraction, and exact citation verification.

decisions.reason: The self-check reports empty output, but the visible final code requests refinement before assigning answer content and readiness. The snapshot ends with constraint-check calls and contains no completed final worker iteration, submission result, or exception. Earlier extraction produced five rows with no local validation failures. This supports an intermediate snapshot with unresolved submission status, not a demonstrated failure requiring a memory; the base prompt already specifies final serialization and readiness.

Both flagged queries returned four hits and recorded no new entities after the initial discovery had already recorded all requested entities. Their results supplied table sources subsequently fetched and used for extraction. The task explicitly required both single and batched search, and no continuing search loop occurred. Neither occurrence establishes a reusable search failure.

The fetching code excludes the singly fetched URL from a deduplicated batch, stores results by URL, and reuses cached text. The worker reports four usable pages, all fetch records succeeded, and grouped extraction produced five rows with no URL, domain, or quote-membership failures. These observed intermediate successes support a narrowly scoped cache skill without claiming final submission succeeded. No existing entries need updating.

proposal.summary: Refine the existing biographical research skill to keep reviews within field scope, and add a memory preventing verification from overwriting stronger evidence. Retain the existing discovery and PDF quotation guidance.

edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads. Give extraction and review calls the same field definition, time frame, and source scope used for the table. Evaluate proposed omissions against that definition before expanding research: when a field concerns affiliations recorded in an award announcement, unrelated advisory roles and undated appointments do not establish omissions. Check completeness within the chosen scope, including secondary institutions and locations.

edits.title: Compare verification results with existing evidence before replacement
edits.content: A follow-up extraction can pass schema and quote-membership checks while losing previously supported parts of a value. Supply verification calls with the existing cell and its supporting evidence as well as new sources. Stage proposed replacements and compare their semantic coverage before mutating accumulated rows. For multivalued fields, investigate any removed component; omission from a shorter source is not evidence that the component is false. A failed corroborating fetch also does not invalidate existing evidence. Retain the stronger supported cell unless new evidence warrants a correction, and revalidate any replacement.

additional_candidates.description: Follow-up verification temporarily replaced a supported multivalued nationality with a narrower value from another person's page.
Broad affiliation audits proposed unrelated appointments; explicitly scoped review separated actual omissions from scope expansion.
An interleaved PDF quotation failed exact membership and was repaired using a stored source slice.

decisions.reason: All 34 occurrences were considered. Signals 0–6 concern annual searches whose inspected results did not explicitly name laureates; subsequent page fetching supplied the roster. Signals 7–31 concern nationality research for already identified people, and signals 32–33 concern follow-up verification of two known people. These searches supplied useful field evidence despite adding no entities. The existing memory explicitly requires honest empty discovery records in these circumstances. Its usage therefore does not demonstrate consistently bad guidance, and the signal count does not justify fabricated discoveries or another edit.

The two failures were distinct backend conditions: Princeton returned HTTP 403, while TAP failed certificate verification. The first was recovered through an already discovered alternative profile; the second left previously fetched institutional evidence available. Neither shows repeated futile retries or supports a host blacklist or transport workaround. The consequential evidence-replacement regression is addressed separately; a generic fetch-failure entry has lower incremental value.

In iteration 10, the verification prompt omitted the existing institutional evidence, and its result reduced an existing three-country value to one country using a navigation listing on another person's page. Schema, coverage, and quote checks still passed. Iteration 11 explicitly restored the stronger original cell. This recovered failure shows why exact quotations alone do not protect semantic completeness and supports a procedural memory without retaining the answer.

The annual audits repeatedly proposed advisory roles and undated appointments beyond the extraction's announcement-based scope, while also finding real missing locations and a former-role qualifier. Subsequent repair instructions and final review explicitly stated the scope, repaired the relevant omissions, and obtained PASS. The existing skill covers field diagnosis and temporal qualifiers but not consistent review scope, so a small extension preserves this successful tactic.

The initial affiliation quote contained the wrong interleaved line. The run inspected stored text, extracted an exact contiguous slice, and verified it before replacement; final citations were verbatim. The existing memory already describes this precise failure and repair, including semantic support and fallback sources. Its observed outcome supports retaining it rather than duplicating or rewriting it.

proposal.summary: Refine discovery identity handling and field-completeness review. Retain existing fetch recovery guidance; the run recovered successfully without repeated failed-URL retries.

edits.title: Inspect results and resolve aliases before recording discoveries
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders caused stalled_search issues even when later calls recorded entities for the same queries. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, do this separately for each query in input order. Do not emit [] before inspection or assume a later record erases an earlier event. Compare entity identities, not only literal name strings: initials, shortened names, and typographic apostrophe variants can refer to already known entities. Maintain evidence-supported aliases and do not count those variants as new discoveries; do not merge ambiguous names without supporting context. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including useful searches that fill missing fields for known entities. Do not invent discoveries to suppress stall warnings.

edits.title: Recover and validate incomplete rendered evidence
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific missing fields before fetching again. Request concise factual summaries for those fields, with brief supporting excerpts where needed, rather than full-page reproduction. Test the revised focus on one page and inspect its evidence before expanding. Preserve each fetched response with its URL and focus so later responses do not overwrite earlier support. Keep unstated fields unresolved and research alternative sources rather than inferring them from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. Validate quotations against an individual saved response and separately review whether the evidence supports the entity, field, relevant time, and required scope. A nonempty value and matching quotation do not establish completeness: track excerpts and summaries as unresolved when the task requires complete exact wording. Check shared statements against their recipient context and distinguish shared from individually assigned claims. Before further retrieval, review all saved evidence for overlooked support; target only remaining gaps. Keep editorial uncertainty notes outside factual values. After repair, repeat quotation checks and a focused semantic review. Match the task's evidence contract: a quotation from rendered text is not thereby authenticated as a quotation from raw source HTML. FETCH_FAILED instead calls for bounded retries and source switching.

additional_candidates.description: Literal name comparison counted variants of known people as new entity discoveries.
Review of saved evidence and targeted retrieval repaired incomplete and misattributed support that passed quotation-membership checks.

decisions.reason: All 16 occurrences concern searches for already known entities: six year-level nationality searches, three targeted affiliation/nationality searches, four individual nationality searches, and three final verification searches. Their empty discovery records are consistent with verification rather than failed discovery; several supplied useful missing-field evidence. The existing memory already permits honest empty records. Repeated signals in its outcome history do not establish consistently bad behavior, and the passing check alone is not the reason for declining.

Reviewed all 21 failures: ten initial Nobel URLs, two early fallback sources, three subsequent nationality sources, two later institutional/news sources, two nationality references, and two final Nature pages. The run reused saved hits, tested a small alternative-source batch, excluded attempted URLs, and recovered usable evidence through other sources, including an alternative CV and a society announcement. Existing memory already covers this behavior and correctly avoids blaming URL suffixes. Its usage outcomes show recovery rather than evidence that the guidance should be deleted or strengthened; isolated failures across different sources do not justify a permanent domain blacklist.

The discovery log records shortened names, added middle initials, and an apostrophe variant as new entities after their full identities were already discovered. The trajectory's literal known_names comparison explains this inflation. Final rows remained deduplicated, so this is a process correction rather than a claim of output failure. Extend the existing discovery memory instead of creating overlapping guidance.

Intermediate quotation checks reported no failures while a motivation remained an excerpt; a later repair even inserted an editorial incompleteness note into its value. Semantic audits identified that gap, overlooked saved support, and misleading shared-recipient framing. Targeted retrieval and corrections resolved them before the final review and deterministic checks passed. Extend the existing incomplete-page skill with this demonstrated review procedure; its empty usage/outcome history provides no basis for deletion or a claim that it caused the earlier defects.

proposal.summary: Clarify semantic review to preserve the requested field meaning and distinguish source excerpts from renderer summaries. Existing memories already cover fetch failures, honest empty discoveries, and evidence reuse.

edits.title: Separate quote membership from factual support
edits.content: A quote occurring in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish source provenance or support for the complete claim. Distinguish actual source excerpts from renderer summaries, generated labels and assembled passages; do not reject a source excerpt solely because it arrived through a renderer. Before recording a positive constraint verdict, verify the entity, requested time period and every substantive component of the value. Keep extraction and audit criteria aligned with the requested field: explicit national descriptors can support nationality without establishing legal citizenship or dual citizenship. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace, flags and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. For composite values, distinguish separately required components from parenthetical organizational descriptions; do not automatically count a parent organization as another affiliation. Treat model audit findings as hypotheses to resolve against saved evidence and the output contract, not instructions to change valid cells. When different sources support different claim components, retain an internal claim-to-excerpt mapping and respect the output contract rather than stitching excerpts into a purported verbatim quote. Recheck semantic support after final mutations, even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

additional_candidates.description: Semantic audits sometimes substituted citizenship for nationality or treated a parent organization as a separately required affiliation; later reviews corrected these interpretations.
Preserving retrieval versions and validating targeted cell patches supported recovery without discarding earlier evidence.
Eight focused citizenship fetches revisited announcements already reported as lacking nationality or citizenship statements and returned the same absence.

decisions.reason: Reviewed all 29 occurrences. Signals 0–3 followed fallback searches whose laureates were already discovered; signals 4–12 followed nationality verification searches; signals 13–23 followed targeted nationality, affiliation and motivation searches; signals 24–28 followed final gap searches. Their empty discoveries did not mean they supplied no useful evidence. Unlike the earlier placeholder failure, this run recorded initial discoveries after inspecting results and used empty lists for known-entity verification. Entry 0 already explicitly permits honest empty discoveries. Its repeated signal counts therefore do not establish consistently bad behavior or justify another edit, independently of the passing self-check.

Reviewed all 26 failures: signals 29–37 cover the uniformly failed nine-page NobelPrize.org batch; 38–43 cover six alternative-page failures; 44–50 cover seven nationality-fetch failures, including repeated LIGO and AP URLs and an APS URL that had previously succeeded; 51–52 cover two institutional pages; 53–54 cover the final EPFL and Scientific American failures. Recovery came through observed successful alternative-host probes and other fetched sources, not through the failed text. The initial batch and repeated URLs remain process problems despite final success, but entry 1 version 2 already addresses probing before expansion, preserving successful results, tracking failed URLs and avoiding unchanged failed batches. Usage records show version 1 was used in this run, so these outcomes do not demonstrate failure of the current revision. No additional host blacklist or causal explanation is supported.

The populated-cell audit demanded explicit citizenship for a nationality column, while later extraction and review correctly accepted explicit national descriptors without asserting dual citizenship. Another audit treated an omitted parenthetical parent organization as a missing affiliation; focused review retained the existing two-institution value. Reviews also inconsistently classified plain rendered excerpts as summaries. These recovered errors support refining entry 3 rather than creating a duplicate. Its core distinction between substring membership and semantic support remains useful: the passing citation and coverage checks cannot settle these interpretation questions.

The run retained page_versions, checked quotations against individual saved retrievals, and validated targeted patches before applying them. This is a successful repeatable tactic, but entry 2 already instructs reuse of saved extraction and fetched text, cell-specific diagnosis, whole-value support checks and validation before mutation. The trajectory supports retaining that entry; a separate skill would substantially duplicate it.

The eight citizenship-focused announcement fetches returned absence already stated in earlier retrievals, so the passing outcome does not erase wasted work. However, a narrower fetch can sometimes clarify an incomplete renderer response, and the run later recovered using biographical and institutional sources. The existing evidence-reuse guidance provides partial coverage; a separate absence-caching rule is less valuable than correcting the demonstrated semantic audit drift and is omitted to keep the harness minimal.
